newsitem.title: GERMANY: German industry orders rise 2.4 pct in January.
newsitem.headline: German industry orders rise 2.4 pct in January.

text.p: Industrial orders in Germany rose 2.4 percent in January from the previous month and were up 4.6 percent from the year-earlier month, the Economics Ministry said on Thursday.
The rises follow a 1.9 percent month-on-month decline in December orders, which were only 1.9 percent higher than the year-earlier month.
Foreign orders, fanned by the weak mark, fueled the rise by gaining 7.3 percent from the previous month. Domestic orders remained in the doldrums, declining 0.8 percent.
Orders in west Germany rose 2.5 percent while east German orders decliend 0.4 percent.
The strong orders figures contrast sharply with industrial output data released on Wednesday showing a 1.7 percent month-on-month decline in January.
The Federation of German Chambers of Industry and Commerce (DIHT) took the gloomier view, saying it believed the economy was stagnating in the current quarter compared to the fourth quarter of 1996.
DIHT said it expected economic growth for the year to reach only two percent, up from 1.4 percent last year but sill less than the government's projection of 2.5 percent growth.
